title: Animating a picture is as simple as setting a moment and changing things: design it, then build it
goal: Animating a picture today starts with choosing a property from a list, and the user does not want to think about properties: they want to move to a moment, change the layer and have that tween on its own, the way the video editor already works. Design one simple way of keying shared by pictures and video, show it to the user as a mock, and build it once they approve.
notes: User, 2026-11-04 (intake): 'The motion pane is totally unintuitive. I hit the + sign and i have to choose which property i want to animate. I do not want to think about this. I want to just start creating keyframes where maybe I position something, save a keyframe, or click on one, adjust some things (opacity position, transform, etc) and it persists on that keyframe and auto tweens. Don't we have this? We should be reusing a lot of the ux for videos for animated images. Please file a task to properly design an intuitive simplified way to create them.' Today: video has Add Key + any change keys itself (Sources/PhotonzCore/KeyMoments.swift, PropertyKeys.swift, LooksAtThePlayhead.swift); pictures lead with the Animate a property picker (Sources/Photonz/EditorState+PropertyKeys.swift, InspectorPanel 'Animate a property'). Related queued: ask-animates-what-it-makes-an-animated-svg-icon (Ask setting keys) should use the same model.
acceptance: DESIGN FIRST, as a mock on the design site (docs/design/mocks/pages/, building on video-animate.html, video-motion.html and icon-animate-wt.html), interactive like the transform modes prototype (pages/selection-transform.html): a picture with a timeline strip; press Add Key (or K) to set a moment; drag, fade, turn and resize the layer and see the key take the change; move the playhead, change it again, see a second key and the tween play; click a key to go to it and change it; delete a key; play and loop. No property picker in the main path.

The design answers, with a recommendation each: where the keyframe strip lives for a picture (the same timeline as video, slimmed); what the Add Key control looks like and its shortcut; how a picture becomes animated (the first Add Key gives it a length and a playhead); how auto-key is shown so a change never keys by surprise (a visible key-moment marker at the playhead, and the change landing on it); easing per key (one simple choice, the video editor's curves under it); and where 'Animate a property' goes (kept only as an Advanced way in, never the first step).

The design REUSES the video editor's key model and controls (KeyMoments, the key line, the value rows that appear only for changed values, the key popover) rather than inventing a second one. Any difference between picture and video needs a reason written down.
Ask the user to review the mock (a decision card with the mock link and a marked screenshot) and wait for approval before building; record their decisions in this log.

BUILD (after approval): an animated picture is made by setting moments and changing things, at Next defaults, with walks for each step of the mock's flow, and the existing animated SVG export carries the result. A person who has never keyed anything can animate a layer moving and fading in under 30 seconds (time it in a walk from first click to playing).
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

Reproduced at Next defaults (/tmp walk: blank, rectangle, Add Motion ▸ Rotation): the only way in is the plus, then a property; it opens a From/To/Around/At/Start/Over/Curve/Repeat form and the strip shows a duration bar with no keys. A drag from the middle of the layer moved the pivot to 640,420 and not the layer.

Design done, no app code touched: docs/design/mocks/pages/picture-keys.html, interactive, in the design site's nav under the icon walkthroughs. Its engine is KeyMoments.swift in miniature and its curves are curve.js. All six answers the checklist asks for are on the page, each with a recommendation, plus a table of what is the video editor's and every difference with its reason.

Checked in the browser with pointer events at real coordinates, plus trusted CDP clicks on the Bell row and Add Key: first key is hollow with no rows; drag at 0:00 fills it and Position appears; ghost diamond after moving the playhead; second key tweens; opacity joins holding 100 at the key before; turn, resize, play, wrap at the end; click a key and change it; delete, undo; Badge with no keys never keys; Curve on a stretch (Ease out back overshoots 437 past a key at 430); cmd-click adds a key; repeats mark cannot cross the last key; last key gone returns to a still, undo restores. That run found and fixed 3 bugs in the prototype: panel frozen during play, strip diamond unclickable because a release rebuilt the rows, landing pop cut off mid-drag.

Chose: picture stays a picture (lap, not a video document) over giving it a duration, because hasTime flips the kind, tool bar and title chip and motionCycleMS already measures a lap. Chose: 2 s, repeating, over today's 0.9 s, because that default is a swing's and a move and a fade need longer. Chose: K only adds and never removes, over the header diamond's toggle, because a double press must not delete work. Chose: a new key takes the curve of the stretch it lands in, and no Easing dropdown in the bar, because the bar has only that one thing to carry on a picture. Chose: the strip lists animated layers plus the picked one, so the picked layer's diamond is always reachable.

Adversarial review before building. (1) A first timer can stall after the first key: nothing says to move the playhead, and pressing play then shows nothing moving. No chrome line allowed for it, so it goes to the tutorial; the 30 second walk must measure it, and the brief asks the user to say if they stall. (2) Two of the user's mocks change under option a (video.html's Animate a property button, icon-animate-wt.html's pivot and Motion list): both are named on the card, neither mock page was edited. (3) The 2026-09-15 card say-where-animating-an-icon-and-editing-a-video answered that motion is a property applied like an effect; this replaces that way in, so it is named in the brief. (4) A Premiere or Photoshop user finds the keys where video has them, but Photoshop's own timeline is not this; the bar is that it is easier, not identical.

For the build, after approval. What the app cannot do yet, all part of this task and nothing to file first: keyLayer, isAnimating, addKeyMoment and keyMomentDiamond guard on hasTime, so keys and hollow moments need a lap path; hasMotionStrip needs a hollow moment to count, since hasMotion only reads motions; foldEditIntoKeys and editLooks do not let new values join outside time (joins = hasTime). The first Add Key writes motionCycleMS = 2000. SVGMotionExport already writes keyTimes and keySplines and has tests for stops (read, not run on a picture made this way). Old From and To motions keep playing. Walks that press Add Motion change with it: icon-export-animated-walk, motion-swings-a-layer-walk, motion-pivot-walk and the rest of grep 'Add Motion' Scripts/playtest. Tutorial text at TutorialGuides.swift:2289 names Animate a property. Space on a picture and the Lens's K need checking on the real app first.

Build: core landed in the working tree, 29 tests green (PictureKeys.swift, Document.keyLap). Chose a stored keyLap plus isKeyedPicture asked from the layers over clearing state on every delete path, because then the last key leaving by any route is a still and undo needs nothing. Chose keys stay .once with a play-time .everyLap over rewriting motions on Repeat, because one source of truth cannot drift. A saved Once on a picture is untouched until someone presses Add Key.

Adversarial pass on the built thing: a still export, Copy and the icon previews read the stored layer, which on a keyed picture is where it was before any key, so a PNG would have shown a place the picture never was. Fixed with keyedStill (first moment) and previews at the playhead. Layers inside a frame were not posed at the playhead, the main case for an icon: failed a test at 4 against 14, fixed with posedTree. Chose first moment for a still over the playhead, because an export should not depend on where the playhead was left. Chose to pin next-picture-keys off on the 14 walks that prove the saved From and To rows, over deleting them, because saved motion still shows those rows and they are the only proof of it.
